title: Design Patterns for AI Trust: Juries, Libraries, and Agent Tiers — Alex Bauer, Upside.tech
talk_summary: Alex Bauer argues that agents should be managed like humans: give them commander's intent (the why), scaffold them with curated anchor documentation instead of YOLO prompting, and use multi-agent juries plus a consensus judge for questions with no single correct answer. He also warns that weak models/harnesses ('tier one' chat products) cannot be fixed by prompting and should be excluded from important work.

takeaways.technique: Anchor assets / curated knowledge base before generation
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to tell it what to know about your business. So, I maintain this list of anchor assets for our entire company

takeaways.technique: Librarian / just-in-time memory with failed-query schema
takeaways.what_they_do: Before answering, the agent consults a 'librarian' that holds docs, knowledge items, and the schema of prior failed queries, returning definitions (e.g., fiscal year, stage thresholds) with citations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the librarian has access to documentation and the library of knowledge items about your company and the schema of prior failed queries

takeaways.technique: Jury + consensus judge for no-ground-truth decisions
takeaways.what_they_do: For questions with no empirically correct answer, spin up independent analysts that each produce evidence-cited opinions; a judge weighs reasoning quality rather than treating outputs as fact, and escalates/expands the jury if consensus is low.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they are going to spin up a team of independent analysts who all look at the data independently and come up with an evidence-cited opinion

takeaways.what_they_do: State why the task matters, not just what to do; explicitly pull agents back from self-micromanagement since they imitate human micromanagement from training data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: tell your agents why you want them to do something, and they will do it a lot better

takeaways.technique: Agent tiers: ban weak harnesses/models for important work
takeaways.what_they_do: Classifies tools into tiers; tier two requires a strong model plus sub-agents, plan mode, full MCP support, and file editing. Anything crowbarred into a cheap subscription plan is excluded from important work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: any AI product where it's been crowbarred into a pre- subscription model is probably not something that you should be using for anything important

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of YOLO 'read everything and produce output', first define the structure/outline (site structure, capability reference), then let the model fill it in; YOLO mode failed even with plan mode.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The step here was define the structure first, and then turn Claude loose. Don't try and YOLO it from the beginning.
